citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
A yellow and green budgerigar in the aviary walked on the ground. When the inspector looked more closely, they saw the
bird holding its left wing lower than its right wing and away from its body and had fecal material present on the tail. As the
inspector continued to observe, the bird chose not to fly; instead, it walked to the wall, climbed the fencing, climbed to a
perch, and then climbed higher fencing to reach an upper perch. When asked whether the bird could fly, the facility
representatives said they did not know and looked at the bird. They then confirmed that it could not fly. When the
inspector asked if they had notified the veterinarian, they said they had not, explaining that they move injured birds that
cannot fly into the barn until they recover, and then return them to the aviary. The facility must perform daily observations
on all animals to assess their health and well being and must maintain direct, frequent communication with the attending
‑
veterinarian to ensure timely and accurate reporting of any health, behavioral, or welfare concerns. Correct by October 9,
2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
